inlines.v: DECE'IVE, verb transitive [L to take asid, to ensnare.] 1. To mislead the mind; to cause to err; to cause to believe what is false, or disbelieve what is true; to impose on; to delude. Take heed that no man deceive you. Matthew 24:4. If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves. 1 John 1:1. 2. To beguile; to cheat. Your father hath deceived me, and changed my wages ten times. 3. To cut off from expectation; to frustrate or disappoint; as, his hopes were deceived. 4. To take from; to rob. Plant fruit trees in large borders, and set therein fine flowers, but thin and sparingly, lest they deceive the trees.
